summary: CairnBio: EU-West production queue-starvation causing degraded embeddings throughput and streaming dark windows
description:
Issue summary: Since ~2026-03-10 06:40 UTC CairnBio (dedicated pool in eu-west) has experienced periodic "dark windows" for streaming responses alongside a sustained drop in embeddings throughput. Customers observed long tail stalls (streaming silence) and ~2-5x increase in embeddings latency and dropped throughput.

Impact: Production traffic for CairnBio (enterprise, dedicated) experienced degraded user-facing latency (SLA exposures for embeddings and streaming SLOs), multiple aborted inference sessions, and a customer-visible decrease in completed embedding requests per second. Billing/exposure risk assessed as moderate until restoration.

Environment: prod | eu-west | dedicated GPU pool id: pool-eu-west-045 | control-plane region: eu-west-1

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 06:38 UTC: Monitoring alerted on embeddings p50/p95 jump for pool-eu-west-045.
- 2026-03-10 06:40 UTC: First customer (CairnBio) Slack escalation to #support; observed streaming silence windows.
- 2026-03-10 07:00 UTC: Support engaged SRE and Oncall; initial mitigation applied (aggressive K/V cache bump, isolated autoscaler override).
- 2026-03-10 08:15 UTC: Partial throughput recovery; intermittent dark windows persist.
- 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC: Second regression observed correlated with short scheduler restarts.
- 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC: Ongoing investigation; secondary mitigations in progress.

Steps to reproduce (customer repro instructions):
1) Send high-concurrency embedding batches (payloads similar to production size) pinned to redwood-emb-1-large in eu-west.
2) Start simultaneous streaming chat sessions pinned to the same dedicated pool.
3) Observe that some streaming sessions see a pause in events (8-20s) while embeddings throttling/queueing increases.

Observed metrics & logs:
- Embeddings P95 latency increased from ~120ms to ~600-1500ms at peak.
- Inflight queue length for pool-eu-west-045 spiked to 1200+ requests.
- Scheduler restarted short-lived worker pods 3x at 02:07 UTC on 2026-03-11; logs show requeue spikes and 'worker backoff' entries.
- Serving-runtime trace excerpts show batch assembly delays and repeated KV cache misses for prefix keys (keyspace: cairn-prod-prefix-*).

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Temporarily increased autoscaler headroom for pool-eu-west-045 to +25% capacity.
- Throttled non-critical background jobs for CairnBio customer routes.
- Applied conservative scheduler patch from PR #5842 to reduce aggressive pod recycling (hotfix rollout to eu-west canaries).

Current status: Recovery partial. Throughput improved but intermittent streaming dark windows remain under load. Active mitigation: coordinated scheduler config rollback in canary regions and scoped KV cache warmup for customer prefixes.

Next steps (short term):
- Complete canary rollout of scheduler patch to all eu-west nodes (owner: Rafael Ortega).
- Implement prefix-aware KV warmup to avoid cold-miss storm during failover (owner: SRE team).
- Add targeted rate-limiter on embedding batch ingestion for CairnBio's route to prevent queue head saturation (owner: API team).

Post-incident follow-up items (for postmortem):
- RCA: investigate root cause between scheduler pod churn and KV cache eviction pattern under the customer's workload.
- SLA remediation plan: evaluate credits for customer if SLA breach confirmed.
- Long-term: refine autoscaler policies for mix of streaming + embedding workloads and add synthetic load tests for dedicated pools.

Notes: Customer is highly sensitive to downtime; assigned CSM engaged and receiving hourly updates. We flagged billing exposure for later reconciliation if duplicate retries inflated counts.
